stills.description: This shaded relief image of Mexico's Yucatán Peninsula shows a subtle, but unmistakable, indication of the Chicxulub impact crater . Most scientists now agree that this impact was the cause of the Cretaceous-Tertiary Extinction , the event 65 million years ago that marked the sudden extinction of the dinosaurs as well as the majority of life then on Earth.

stills.description: http://www2.jpl.nasa.gov/files/images/captions/p45062.txt : Chicxulub impact site December 28, 1994 This painting by Donald E. Davis depicts an asteroid slamming into tropical, shallow seas of the sulfur-rich Yucatan Peninsula in what is today southeast Mexico. The aftermath of this immense asteroid collision, which occurred approximately 65 million years ago, is believed to have caused the extinction of the dinosaurs and many other species on Earth.
